reference_items.figure_description:
Six 2D polygon outlines arranged in two rows of three:
- Top row:
  - P: a scalene triangle with a horizontal base.
  - Q: a four-sided quadrilateral resembling a trapezoid, with horizontal top and bottom sides (top shorter than bottom) and slanted right side.
  - R: a diamond/rhombus shape (a square rotated 45 degrees).
- Bottom row:
  - S: a very wide, flat obtuse triangle with a horizontal top-like orientation and a vertex pointing down.
  - T: an isosceles trapezoid with parallel horizontal top and bottom edges (top shorter than bottom).
  - U: a wide obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge and a vertex pointing downwards.

Which two figures are congruent?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectilinear figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: An L-shaped polygon with a horizontal top arm extending to the right and a vertical arm on the left extending downwards.
- Figure 2: A large rectangular/square shape with a small rectangular tab extending out to the upper right.
- Figure 3: An L-shaped polygon with a tall vertical left arm and a shorter horizontal bottom arm extending to the right.
- Figure 4: An L-shaped polygon with a horizontal bottom arm extending to the left and a vertical arm on the right extending upwards, having the same arm lengths and thickness as Figure 1 rotated 180 degrees.

reference_items.figure_description:
A line drawing of a scene containing geometric elements:
- In the upper right sky, a circular shape is labeled "sun" with a line drawn to the label "circle".
- Behind the house are trees rendered with leafy texture.
- In the center is a two-story house:
  - The roof features two dormers, each topped with a triangular roof and containing a rectangular window divided into four square panes.
  - A small chimney is on the roof ridge.
  - The main facade is rectangular, featuring two rectangular windows (each divided into four panes) and a central rectangular front door.
  - The door contains a diamond-shaped (rhombus) window and a small round doorknob.
- In front of the door is a stone path composed of trapezoidal and triangular paving stones.
- To the lower left of the house stands a lamppost consisting of a circular light mounted on a tall, narrow rectangular post set in grass.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: four angles varied in size and labeled P, Q, R, and S from left to right.]

In which of the following are the angles ordered by size, from least to greatest?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four angles are shown side by side, labeled from left to right as P, Q, R, and S. Each angle has a horizontal ray pointing to the right, a second ray extending from the left endpoint, and a curved arc indicating the angle between the two rays:
- Angle P is an acute angle opening upward and to the right at approximately 45°.
- Angle Q is an obtuse angle opening upward and to the left at approximately 120°.
- Angle R is a right angle (90°) formed with a vertical ray extending straight up.
- Angle S is an acute angle opening upward and to the right at approximately 30°, smaller than angle P.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

C.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure that is not the same shape as the one you made in Part B
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors: Any of four figures (6-sided) that was not used in part B.
Repeats a correct figure already given in part B
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part C response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three arrangements of 3 tiles labeled Rita, Ina, and Lana]

Rita, Ina, and Lana take turns arranging 3 tiles. Each arranges the tiles in a different shape as shown above. Which of the following is true about the area of the shapes?

options.label: A
options.text: Rita’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: B
options.text: Ina’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: C
options.text: Lana’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: D
options.text: All of the shapes have the same area.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three arrangements of three tiles each, labeled "Rita", "Ina", and "Lana":
- Rita: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. A triangle sits on top of the left square, with its base along the top edge of that square and its apex pointing upward.
- Ina: A square sits at the top with horizontal top and bottom edges. Attached below it is a triangle sharing the square's bottom horizontal edge and pointing downward. Attached to the lower-right edge of the triangle is a second square, tilted diagonally downward and to the right.
- Lana: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. Attached to the right vertical edge of the right square is a triangle pointing to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top is an equilateral triangle with dots at each of its three vertices, labeled "tile" to the right of its right edge.

Below is an irregular polygon drawn on an isometric (triangular) dot grid, with dots marking vertices along its boundary and in its interior:
- Top edge: a horizontal segment 3 units long, with 4 dots evenly spaced (including endpoints).
- Left boundary: from the top-left dot, a line goes down and right by 1 unit to an indented vertex dot; from there, a line goes down and left by 1 unit to the bottom-left corner dot.
- Bottom edge: a horizontal segment 4 units long, with 5 dots evenly spaced (including endpoints).
- Right boundary: from the top-right dot, a line goes down and right by 1 unit to a vertex dot at the middle horizontal level; from that dot, a horizontal line extends right by 1 unit to another vertex dot; from that dot, a line goes down and left by 1 unit to the bottom-right corner dot.
- Interior: 2 dots are spaced along the middle horizontal level between the left indented vertex and the right boundary.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
